children.name: Video - Debug Mode — Tars canvas with active gambit highlighted
Asimov is Tars' AI agent for Slack. Work kept starting in Slack threads and finishing somewhere else, so we wanted the agent to handle that second half.
children.characters: Asimov is Tars' AI agent for Slack. Work kept starting in Slack threads and finishing somewhere else, so we wanted the agent to handle that second half.

children.name: I took it from a thread summarizer to an AI teammate inside Slack, creating experiences for knowledge management, app integrations and configuring automated workflows.
children.characters: I took it from a thread summarizer to an AI teammate inside Slack, creating experiences for knowledge management, app integrations and configuring automated workflows.

children.name: The product began with a single capability: summarizing Slack threads. Each release expanded what Asimov could understand, connect to and eventually do on a team's behalf.
children.characters: The product began with a single capability: summarizing Slack threads. Each release expanded what Asimov could understand, connect to and eventually do on a team's behalf.

children.name: Teams connected sources like Notion and Google Drive so Asimov could answer from company docs, with sync status and refresh timing visible for each source.
children.characters: Teams connected sources like Notion and Google Drive so Asimov could answer from company docs, with sync status and refresh timing visible for each source.

children.name: One place to connect an app, see what it's linked to and what information Asimov is accessing from it.
children.characters: One place to connect an app, see what it's linked to and what information Asimov is accessing from it.

children.name: Teams configured third-party app actions and built custom ones that, combined with Slack context, enabled Asimov to automate recurring workflows.
children.characters: Teams configured third-party app actions and built custom ones that, combined with Slack context, enabled Asimov to automate recurring workflows.

children.name: I interviewed customer success, sales, engineering, design and marketing to understand how work moved across conversations, tools and teams.
children.characters: I interviewed customer success, sales, engineering, design and marketing to understand how work moved across conversations, tools and teams.

children.name: Rather than validating a specific feature, I wanted to identify where an AI teammate could meaningfully participate in daily work and boost productivity.
children.characters: Rather than validating a specific feature, I wanted to identify where an AI teammate could meaningfully participate in daily work and boost productivity.

children.name: Opportunity 1: Work happened across multiple tools
children.characters: Opportunity 1: Work happened across multiple tools

children.name: Slack conversations often triggered work elsewhere. Customer-facing teams moved from a discussion to updating HubSpot, writing reports or sharing project updates, often times carrying the same context across multiple tools. Summaries reduced reading time, but rarely reduced the work that followed.

children.name: Engineering wanted GitHub workflows, sales wanted CRM updates and marketing wanted content generation. The pattern that emerged was a need for flexibility. Instead of designing automations for every use case, we designed a system that let teams define their own actions on top of connected tools.

Engineering wanted GitHub workflows, sales wanted CRM updates and marketing wanted content generation. The pattern that emerged was a need for flexibility.
Instead of designing automations for every use case, we designed a system that let teams define their own actions on top of connected tools.

children.name: Setup took three steps: connect Slack, add knowledge sources and choose what Asimov could access.

children.name: No fixed set of actions could cover every team's workflow, so I designed a system where teams decided what Asimov could do.

children.name: Early versions focused on what Asimov could do. As it grew, the question became who should be allowed to configure it.

children.name: Full role-based permissions needed backend work beyond the beta timeline. I designed the future access model and used Slack's admin permissions in the meantime.
